note: Verified against legislation.qld.gov.au on 2026-08-14. The UCPR contains no time-reckoning rule of its own: the note to r 7 states that a time allowed or provided for under the rules is calculated according to the Acts Interpretation Act 1954 s 38, which applies to the UCPR through the Statutory Instruments Act 1992 s 14(1) and sch 1 (item 'parts 9-11'). The UCPR dictionary is schedule 3 and adopts the AIA sch 1 'business day' definition. Rollover under s 38(2) turns on 'excluded days' — for filing, days the registry is closed (s 38(5)(a)), and the registry closes on Saturdays, Sundays and court holidays (r 976); the script approximates registry-closed days with the weekend-and-public-holiday table, and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the registry was open.

computation_provisions.summary: Reckoning of time: a period beginning on a day, act or event excludes that day (s 38(1)), and a period of clear days or of at least a specified number of days also excludes the day on which the purpose is to be fulfilled (s 38(1)(a)); where the time or last day falls on an excluded day it moves to the next day that is not an excluded day (s 38(2)); 'excluded day' means, for filing or registering a document, a day the office is closed, and otherwise a day that is not a business day in the place (s 38(5)); 'business day' (sch 1) excludes Saturdays, Sundays and public, special and bank holidays.

computation_provisions.citation: Statutory Instruments Act 1992 (Qld) s 14(1) and sch 1
computation_provisions.summary: Applies the provisions of the Acts Interpretation Act 1954 mentioned in sch 1 — including parts 9-11, which carry s 38, and the sch 1 dictionary with 'business day' — to statutory instruments such as the UCPR in the same way as they apply to an Act (s 14(1)). The UCPR is a rule and hence a statutory instrument (s 7(3)); the note to UCPR r 7 confirms the s 38 calculation basis.

period_rules.label: Notice of intention to defend (with defence attached) after service of claim
period_rules.trigger: Service of the claim on the defendant; the period runs after the day the claim is served
warnings: The defence must be attached to the notice of intention to defend (r 139(1)(b)), so this deadline is also the effective defence deadline.

Where the Service and Execution of Process Act 1992 (Cwlth) applies to interstate service, the time limited by that Act displaces the 28 days (r 137(2)); where the claim was served outside Australia under ch 4 pt 7, r 129(3) substitutes 42 days unless the court orders otherwise.
A defendant may file a notice of intention to defend at any time before judgment even if in default (r 138), subject to the default-judgment consequences.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed Queensland public holiday; for filing, an excluded day under AIA s 38(5)(a) is a day the registry is closed, and the registry closes on court holidays (r 976), which may differ from gazetted public holidays — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

period_rules.label: Notice of appeal to the Court of Appeal
period_rules.trigger: The date of the decision appealed from; 'decision' means an order, judgment, verdict or an assessment of damages (r 744)
warnings: The period applies unless the Court of Appeal orders otherwise — the dispensing power sits in r 748 itself, and the general extension power in r 7(1) also remains available.
Where leave to appeal is required, r 747(2) fixes additional content requirements for the notice; this entry does not compute any leave-application deadline.
The notice of appeal is filed with the registrar of the Supreme Court at Brisbane (r 746(1)); the holiday table is Brisbane-area based — confirm registry-location holidays.
